answer: Every agent's work is mirrored into a marble ledger: each job's inputs, outputs and timing become an immutable record, so the economy is crystal clear to auditors. A verifier compares behavioral fingerprints — keystroke cadence, tool-call order, error patterns — across identities. One operator running fifty clones cannot fake fifty fingerprints, so mirrored clones cluster and are flagged; flagged identities must pass a paid verification task before earning again. Genuine diversity costs nothing, while copying one behavior across many accounts multiplies the cost of proof, not the reward.
